name: Wisconsin
headline_status: Marijuana is illegal; only non-psychoactive CBD is allowed with a physician's certification.
summary: Wisconsin has no medical or recreational marijuana law. A first possession offense is a misdemeanor, and a repeat offense can be charged as a felony. Since 2017, anyone with a physician's written certification may possess non-psychoactive CBD. A Republican-led medical cannabis bill cleared a Senate committee in late 2025 but never got a floor vote, and Wisconsin has no citizen-initiative process, so any change has to come from the Legislature.

medical_program.value: CBD-only. Since 2017 Act 4, people with a physician's written certification may possess CBD in a non-psychoactive form for any medical condition. Growing cannabis to make it is not allowed.

penalties.value: A first possession offense is a misdemeanor (up to 6 months in jail and/or a $1,000 fine). A subsequent offense is a felony (up to 3.5 years and/or a $10,000 fine).

retail_sales.value: No legal marijuana sales; Wisconsin lacks medical, decriminalization and legalization laws.

possession_limit.value: No amount of marijuana is legal to possess. A first offense is a misdemeanor with up to 6 months in jail and/or a $1,000 fine.

purchase_age.value: No legal purchase of marijuana for any age; there are no licensed adult-use or medical marijuana sales.

public_use.value: Not allowed anywhere: there is no legal recreational or medical marijuana use, so using it in public or private can lead to possession charges.

tourists.value: No. There are no legal marijuana sales, out-of-state medical cards are not recognized, and visitors face the same possession penalties as residents.

home_grow.value: Not allowed; cultivating marijuana is a felony.

dui.value: Zero tolerance: Wisconsin is among the states that ban driving with any amount of THC or its metabolites in the body, even without proof of impairment.

timeline.event: Gov. Scott Walker signs AB 726, allowing CBD for seizure disorders.
2017 Act 4 extends CBD possession to anyone with a physician's certification.
Local advisory referendums show strong support for medical and adult-use cannabis.
A medical cannabis bill from Senate President Mary Felzkowski clears committee but gets no floor vote.

faq.a: No. Wisconsin has no recreational or medical marijuana law, and possession can bring jail time.
Yes, in non-psychoactive form for people with a physician's written certification.

faq.q: Can Wisconsin voters legalize cannabis at the ballot?
faq.a: No. Wisconsin has no statewide citizen-initiative process, so legalization would have to pass the Legislature.
